# blakstrip

> A private, in-browser PDF redactor that removes content instead of covering it. Everything runs locally, nothing is uploaded, and it verifies the result before you download.

blakstrip renders your PDF in the browser with pdf.js and rasterizes the pages you redact, so the underlying text, vectors, and hidden layers are gone rather than sitting behind a black box. Before export it audits what is hiding in the file (author metadata, XMP, annotations, form-field values, embedded JavaScript, attachments) and strips all of it; after export it re-inspects the output and shows you exactly what is still recoverable. A strict Content-Security-Policy (`connect-src 'none'`) blocks all network egress, verifiable in devtools, and the app works fully offline as a PWA.

## Tools

- [Redact a PDF](https://blakstrip.com/pdf-redact): Drop a PDF, draw boxes or search a term and redact every instance, then export a cleaned file. Audits hidden data on load and verifies the output before download.

## About

- [Home](https://blakstrip.com/): What blakstrip is, and why removing content is different from covering it.

## Notes

- All processing is client-side. No files are uploaded, and no analytics are collected.
- Redacted pages are rasterized (their text becomes an image); untouched pages keep selectable text.
- Built by sixra.dev (https://sixra.dev)
